What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I don't know, it depends on your interests. I think my Field Full of Folk course was interesting, but more demanding. In general I think the first year courses are quite a lot easier than the first year courses at the University of Copenhagen. Because people in Edinburgh are younger when they start uni, the first year seems to be a bridge between high school and uni. So, if you want more of a challenge, go for courses in second year and above, but it can also be nice to have less academically challenging courses when abroad.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Enjoy the welcoming and outgoing nature of Scots! It is easier to socialize with strangers than in Denmark
2) Start looking for accommodation early. It can be hard to find
3) Explore the societies at the university, they contain a lot of fun opportunities

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the historical settings and beautiful nature!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting nice people, getting a new perspective on the Danish education system by seeing another.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The students are a lot younger than in Denmark, it can sometimes be difficult to relate to them. Not a challenge as such, just something to be prepared for. Actually, the biggest challenge might have been the process of finding available courses, this was very difficult, especially as a student in the humanities. So please have patience.
